title: Fibrant targets detect weak equivalences using specified very good cylinders
statement:
Use model categories, cofibrant and fibrant objects, and trivial fibrations from [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. Let $\mathcal M$ be a model category with classes $(C,F,W)$, let $A,B$ be cofibrant objects, and let $u:A\to B$ be any morphism. For each $T\in\{A,B\}$ choose a factorization of the codiagonal
$$T\amalg T\xrightarrow{j_T}I_T\xrightarrow{p_T}T$$
with $j_T$ a cofibration and $p_T$ a trivial fibration (a very good cylinder for $T$); write $e_{T,k}=j_T\mathrm{in}_k$ for $k=0,1$, so $p_Te_{T,k}=1_T$. For every fibrant object $Z$, define $h_I(T,Z)$ to be $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal M}(T,Z)$ modulo the equivalence relation generated by pairs $(H e_{T,0},H e_{T,1})$ for morphisms $H:I_T\to Z$. Precomposition with $u$ induces a well-defined function
$$u^*:h_I(B,Z)\longrightarrow h_I(A,Z),\qquad [b]\longmapsto[b u].$$
For every such choice of the two factorizations, $u\in W$ if and only if $u^*$ is bijective for every fibrant $Z$. No simplicial enrichment, properness, or fibrancy of $A$ or $B$ is assumed.

source.place: A. Joyal, The theory of quasi-categories and its applications (CRM Barcelona, 2008), Appendix E, Proposition E.1.10, proof on printed p. 431: the h(u,X) criterion for cofibrant A,B and fibrant X; justified by Propositions E.1.4 and E.1.8. No Stacks tag.

proof.text: Work in enlarged universes and choose an ordinary localization $\gamma:\mathcal M\to\mathcal H$ at $W$, with the conventions of [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test]. For each $T=A,B$, the map $p_T$ is a trivial fibration, hence lies in $F\cap W$, while $j_T$ is a cofibration and $p_Te_{T,k}=1_T$. Thus this is a good cylinder in the sense of that node. For a fibrant $Z$, factor its diagonal as a trivial cofibration followed by a fibration to choose a good path object, using the model weak factorization systems in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test]. Every generating pair of the relation defining $h_I(T,Z)$ has equal localization images. Equality of localization images is an equivalence relation, so it contains the generated equivalence relation. Conversely, if $\gamma(f)=\gamma(g)$, the cited fixed-cylinder criterion, with cofibrant source $T$ and fibrant target $Z$, supplies a single $H:I_T\to Z$ with endpoints $f,g$. Thus two maps have the same class in $h_I(T,Z)$ if and only if their localization images agree.

source.place: Appendix E, Proposition E.1.10, proof of the h(u,X) criterion; comparison of a chosen very good cylinder with localized homotopy.

proof.text: For every fibrant Z and T=A,B, define Φ_{T,Z}:h_I(T,Z)→Hom_H(γT,γZ) by Φ_{T,Z}([f])=γ(f). Step 1 gives well-definedness and injectivity. Since T is cofibrant and Z is fibrant, [lem-coef-model-localization-map-surjective] says that every morphism γT→γZ is γ(f) for some f:T→Z, so Φ_{T,Z} is surjective and therefore bijective.

source.place: Appendix E, Proposition E.1.10, identification of h(-,X) with localized Hom-sets.

proof.text: First check the asserted quotient map. If $[b]=[b']$ in $h_I(B,Z)$, Step 1 gives $\gamma(b)=\gamma(b')$, hence $\gamma(bu)=\gamma(b)\gamma(u)=\gamma(b')\gamma(u)=\gamma(b'u)$. Step 1 for $A$ then gives $[bu]=[b'u]$, so $u^*([b])=[bu]$ is well-defined. The bijections from Step 2 satisfy $\Phi_{A,Z}(u^*[b])=\gamma(bu)=\Phi_{B,Z}([b])\gamma(u)$. Hence $u^*$ is bijective exactly when precomposition by $\gamma(u)$ is bijective on the corresponding localized Hom-sets. This proves the required compatibility directly, without assuming a map between the chosen cylinders.

source.place: Appendix E, Proposition E.1.10, naturality of the h(u,X) map.

proof.text: If u∈W, then γ(u) is an isomorphism because γ is an ordinary localization at W. Precomposition with an isomorphism is a bijection on every Hom-set, so Step 3 and the bijections Φ show that u^* is bijective for every fibrant Z.

source.place: Appendix E, Proposition E.1.10, forward implication.

proof.text: Conversely, suppose $u^*$ is bijective for every fibrant $Z$. By Steps 2–3, precomposition with $\gamma(u)$ is bijective from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal H}(\gamma B,\gamma Z)$ to $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal H}(\gamma A,\gamma Z)$ for every fibrant $Z$. Using the functorial factorizations of terminal maps in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test], choose trivial-cofibration fibrant replacements $t_A:A\to RA$ and $t_B:B\to RB$. Their localization images are isomorphisms. Surjectivity at $RA$ gives $\alpha:\gamma B\to\gamma RA$ with $\alpha\gamma(u)=\gamma(t_A)$. Put $v=\gamma(t_A)^{-1}\alpha$; then $v\gamma(u)=1_{\gamma A}$. The two maps $\beta=\gamma(t_B)$ and $\beta'=\gamma(t_B)\gamma(u)v$ from $\gamma B$ to $\gamma RB$ satisfy $\beta'\gamma(u)=\gamma(t_B)\gamma(u)v\gamma(u)=\gamma(t_B)\gamma(u)=\beta\gamma(u)$. Injectivity at $RB$ gives $\beta'=\beta$. Cancelling the isomorphism $\gamma(t_B)$ yields $\gamma(u)v=1_{\gamma B}$. Thus $\gamma(u)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Appendix E, Proposition E.1.10, converse reduction and construction of the inverse in the localization.

proof.text: We reflect this localization isomorphism directly, without invoking a localization-detection theorem. The lifting-class descriptions in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] imply closure of $C$ and $F$ under composition: a left lift against a composite of right-class maps is obtained by lifting first against the second map and then the first, while a lift from a composite of left-class maps is obtained in the order first map, then second map. Isomorphisms, in particular identities, are in $C\cap W$ because they have the left lifting property against every fibration. Let $R$ be the functorial fibrant replacement from Step 5 and put $f=R(u):RA\to RB$. Both $RA,RB$ are cofibrant, since their initial maps are the composites $0\to A\to RA$ and $0\to B\to RB$ of cofibrations, and fibrant by construction. Naturality gives $f t_A=t_Bu$, so $\gamma(f)$ is an isomorphism. Factor $f$ as $RA\xrightarrow{i}E\xrightarrow{p}RB$, with $i$ a trivial cofibration and $p$ a fibration. The composites $0\to RA\to E$ and $E\to RB\to1$ show that $E$ is cofibrant and fibrant. Since $\gamma(i)$ and $\gamma(f)$ are isomorphisms, so is $\gamma(p)$.

source.place: Appendix E, Proposition E.1.4 (printed p. 429), expanded by an agent using the model axioms and the cited Mathlib fundamental-lemma interfaces; this supplies the localization reflection used in the proof of Proposition E.1.10 (printed p. 431).

proof.text: By [lem-coef-model-localization-map-surjective], with cofibrant source $RB$ and fibrant target $E$, choose $s:RB\to E$ with $\gamma(s)=\gamma(p)^{-1}$. Choose a very good cylinder $RB\amalg RB\to J\xrightarrow{c}RB$ with endpoints $j_0,j_1$. The fixed-cylinder criterion in [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test] gives $H:J\to RB$ with $Hj_0=ps$ and $Hj_1=1_{RB}$. The injection $\mathrm{in}_0:RB\to RB\amalg RB$ is a cofibration: for a square against any trivial fibration, keep the prescribed lift on the first summand, lift the map on the second summand using the cofibration $0\to RB$, and assemble the two maps by the coproduct property. Composing this injection with the cylinder cofibration makes $j_0$ a cofibration. Since $cj_0=1_{RB}$ and $c\in W$, two-out-of-three gives $j_0\in W$. Apply the model lifting axiom to the square with left map $j_0$, right map $p$, top map $s$ and bottom map $H$. It yields $V:J\to E$ with $Vj_0=s$ and $pV=H$. Put $t=Vj_1$. Then $pt=1_{RB}$, and invertibility of $\gamma(p)$ implies $\gamma(t)=\gamma(p)^{-1}$ and $\gamma(tp)=1_{\gamma E}$.

source.place: Appendix E, Proposition E.1.4 (printed p. 429), expanded by an agent using the model axioms and the cited Mathlib fundamental-lemma interfaces; this supplies the localization reflection used in the proof of Proposition E.1.10 (printed p. 431).

proof.text: Choose a very good cylinder $E\amalg E\to K\xrightarrow{c_E}E$ with endpoints $k_0,k_1$. Applying [lem-coef-localized-good-homotopy-test] to the cofibrant source and fibrant target $E$ and the equality $\gamma(tp)=\gamma(1_E)$ gives $G:K\to E$ with $Gk_0=tp$ and $Gk_1=1_E$. Since $c_Ek_j=1_E$ and $c_E\in W$, two-out-of-three gives $k_0,k_1\in W$. From $Gk_1=1_E$ it gives $G\in W$, and therefore $tp=Gk_0\in W$. In the arrow category the map from $p:E\to RB$ to $tp:E\to E$ has source component $1_E$ and target component $t$; the reverse map has source component $1_E$ and target component $p$. The commutativity equations are $tp=tp$ and $ptp=p$, and their composite on $p$ is $(1_E,pt)=(1_E,1_{RB})$. Thus $p$ is an arrow retract of $tp$, so retract closure of $W$ in [lem-coef-simplicial-boundary-collapse-test] gives $p\in W$. Consequently $f=pi\in W$. Finally, $f t_A=t_Bu$ with $t_A,t_B\in W$ gives $u\in W$ by two-out-of-three, completing the converse.

split_report.summary: Eight-step proof of the Joyal E.1.10 fibrant-target criterion. Identifies the quotient for each prescribed cylinder with localized Hom-sets, proves precomposition well-defined, constructs a two-sided inverse using fibrant replacements, and reflects it directly by a cylinder lift and an explicit arrow retract. Does not cite the general localization-detection node, whose dependency closure reaches this item. No new nodes; statement unchanged.
